title: Fourier concentration from switching failure bounds
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Suppose $f$ has a DNF representation of width at most the positive integer $w$, and let $0<\varepsilon\le1$. Assume that for every nonnegative integer $d$, the probability that a random restriction with retention parameter $1/(10w)$ leaves decision-tree depth at least $d$ is at most $(1/2)^d$. Then the sum of squared Fourier coefficients of the real-valued version of $f$ over subsets of coordinates of size greater than $30w\lceil\log_2(3/\varepsilon)\rceil$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
